heroHeadline: China Earns $500M/Hour from AI-Supercharged Exports (Bloomberg); Trump Flies to Beijing with Musk, Cook & Fink — AI Deconfliction Channel Tops May 14–15 Summit Agenda
heroSubtitle: Bloomberg reported May 12 that China is earning approximately $500 million per hour from exports supercharged by AI adoption across manufacturing and logistics — a framing of China's April 2026 trade data (exports +14.1% YoY vs +7.1% forecast; imports +25.3% vs +16.1% forecast) that directly challenges the export control strategy's effectiveness narrative. Goldman Sachs and Nomura estimate AI hardware and semiconductors account for ~50% of export growth. South China Morning Post published a companion analysis titled 'China's AI Ascent Leaves Trump a Stark Choice: Escalate or Relax Chip Controls' — framing the Trump-Xi summit as a binary decision point. Trump departed for Beijing on May 11 with a high-profile tech CEO delegation: Elon Musk (xAI/Tesla), Tim Cook (Apple), and Larry Fink (BlackRock). The US's primary tech objective is establishing a dedicated AI 'deconfliction' channel to prevent autonomous military AI misunderstandings from escalating — the first formal US-China AI governance dialogue proposed under the Trump administration. Stanford AI Index confirmed the US-China AI performance gap has 'effectively closed' (39 Arena benchmark points, down from 1,300+ in May 2023), adding urgency from the US side. Cook's inclusion reflects Apple's acute supply chain exposure — Foxconn Zhengzhou produces ~50% of global iPhones — while Commerce Secretary Lutnick's promised 'semiconductor sectoral tariffs' hang over the electronics sector. This pre-summit week also saw SMIC founder Richard Chang argue (May 11, TrendForce) that 80% of global chip demand lies outside advanced nodes where China cannot yet compete, validating China's mature-node dominance strategy. Moonshot AI raised $2B at a $20B valuation (led by Meituan, with Alibaba and Tencent) — joining DeepSeek ($45B), MiniMax ($40B+), and Zhipu AI ($14B) as China's fourth AI unicorn in 2026. China's AI self-reliance stack — Huawei Ascend hardware (60% domestic market share), DeepSeek/Doubao/ERNIE models ($45B/120T-token/day valuations), Moonshot Kimi ($20B), ByteDance $29.4B capex, and CATL battery dominance — is accelerating on every layer simultaneously as the most consequential US-China tech summit in years opens on May 14.
